answer: Cross-Epoch Signature Divergence Rule. Each identity signs a random challenge at epochs' ledge; the system retains a compressed sketch of its signing cadence and phrasing baseline. A returning identity must produce an echo of that baseline within tolerance, or its accumulated history is voided. Attackers must maintain every sybil across epochs, paying continuous signing and storage costs plus failed revalidation losses. A single epoch of mismatched cadence snaps the quill: history resets to zero.
